patch.summary: Two numbers set your GetResponse invoice, and only one of them is on the pricing page: your contact band, and the number of automation workflows you need. The second is the wall most buyers hit first — starter limited to 1 custom automation workflow and capped AI generator uses. Published tiers, at their entry-band floors: Free ($0/mo) · Starter ($19/mo) · Marketer ($59/mo) · Creator ($69/mo) · Enterprise (quote only). Free exists but is deliberately narrow: Free plan heavily limited after 14-day premium window (branding, LP visits, automation filters). And several tools people assume are included are not: SMS, dedicated IP/domain, and some enterprise tools require Enterprise.

seo.title: GetResponse Plans: List-Size Bands and the Starter Wall
seo.description: Price GetResponse on two axes: contact band and workflow count. Starter limited to 1 custom automation workflow and capped AI generator uses. Higher tiers unlock webinars, SMS, and dedicated sending.

sections.heading: The workflow count is the real wall, not the contact band
sections.body: Contact bands move gradually — you grow into the next one. The workflow limit does not: Starter limited to 1 custom automation workflow and capped AI generator uses. So the question that decides your tier is a small one you can answer today: do you need a second automation? An abandoned-cart flow plus a welcome sequence is already two, which means the plan jumps before your list does. Teams who budget only for band growth get surprised in week three by a limit that has nothing to do with list size.

sections.heading: Which tools are locked behind which tier
sections.body: Webinars and course tooling sit on the creator-oriented rung, so if teaching is your acquisition channel your tier is chosen for you. Meanwhile SMS, dedicated IP/domain, and some enterprise tools require Enterprise — which matters because dedicated sending infrastructure is exactly what high-volume senders assume comes with a paid plan. The workflow advantage of the higher rungs is that acquisition, delivery, and follow-up run in the same place: a webinar registration can trigger a nurture path without an integration in between, whereas splitting those across tools means someone maintains the join.

sections.heading: What free actually gives you, and where this stops
sections.body: Read the free tier honestly: Free plan heavily limited after 14-day premium window (branding, LP visits, automation filters). It is a genuine starting point for a small list, not a long-term plan, and the branding and page limits arrive precisely when you start to care. Then the category boundary: Not a full sales CRM — email/automation center of gravity. That is a poor fit warning, not a criticism — if you need deal stages and forecast, keep a CRM and let this drive lifecycle communication. Migration risk sits mostly in list reputation and field mapping; moving an engaged list is never just an export and an import.
sections.tip: Count your workflows before you compare contact bands.

blocks.body: Choose a GetResponse tier by counting automation workflows first and contact band second — one workflow is the entry limit, and webinars, SMS, and dedicated sending each sit on specific higher rungs.

blocks.heading: Write the workflow list and count it
blocks.body: Welcome sequence, abandoned cart, re-engagement, post-purchase upsell — each one is a workflow that has to run at the same time as the others. Write the list, count it, and compare against the entry-tier limit. This single count decides more of your invoice than your list size will for the first year.

blocks.heading: Circle the tools you assumed were included
blocks.body: Go through your plan for the year and circle anything that needs webinars, SMS, or dedicated sending infrastructure. Each circle points at a specific rung. Discovering one of these after purchase is the classic mid-year upgrade nobody budgeted for.
blocks.tip: If webinars are your acquisition channel, your tier is already chosen.

blocks.heading: Price the band from a pruned list, on the live selector
blocks.body: Published headline figures are floors at a small list size; your real number comes from the plan selector at your actual pruned contact count. Prune first — unengaged contacts cost you band space and deliverability together — then read the price for the number that is left, not the number you started with.
